question: Using a suitable property of definite integrals, evaluate $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{x}{(\sin x+\cos x)^2}\,dx$ without first finding an indefinite integral of the complete integrand.
explanation:
Let

$$I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{x}{(\sin x+\cos x)^2}\,dx$$

Use the property $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\int_a^b f(a+b-x)\,dx$. Here, $a=0$ and $b=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Therefore,

$$I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\frac{\pi}{2}-x}{\left[\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)+\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)\right]^2}\,dx$$

Since $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)=\cos x$ and $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)=\sin x$, this becomes

$$I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\frac{\pi}{2}-x}{(\sin x+\cos x)^2}\,dx$$

Adding this expression to the original expression for $I$,

$$2I=\frac{\pi}{2}\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{dx}{(\sin x+\cos x)^2}$$

Now, $\sin x+\cos x=\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$. Hence,

$$\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{dx}{(\sin x+\cos x)^2}=\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\csc^2\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)dx$$

Therefore,

$$=\frac{1}{2}\left[-\cot\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}$$

$$=\frac{1}{2}\left[-\cot\frac{3\pi}{4}+\cot\frac{\pi}{4}\right]=\frac{1}{2}[1+1]=1$$

Thus,

$$2I=\frac{\pi}{2}$$

and hence

$$I=\frac{\pi}{4}$$

Therefore, $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{x}{(\sin x+\cos x)^2}\,dx=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
